definition_used: When a journal/publisher/author/third party uses the phrase “legal reasons,” documents litigation or legal threats, or mentions one or more specific laws
caution: Legal reasons are a broad signal of external process, not directly indicating a specific manuscript integrity problem; main figure not recommended as it is a status/process notice.
semantic_rationale: The definition describes legal reasons or threats as a process signal involving litigation or laws, which relates to post-publication oversight and due process, but does not inherently confirm a problem with research content, authorship, or editorial governance.
